message.content: {"facts":[{"fact_id":"F1","status":"VERIFIED","reason":"Both OpenStax passages directly state S-phase DNA replication yields identical sister chromatids firmly attached at the centromeric/centromere region; organism scope (eukaryotic, S phase) matches. Two pages same publisher, so treated as one source, not independent cross-validation.","evidence_ids":["E_70c6108994","E_d79c940d49"]},{"fact_id":"F2","status":"VERIFIED","reason":"E_70c6108994 says centrosome duplicated during S phase and two centrosomes give rise to mitotic spindle; E_d79c940d49 says centrosome duplication completed in G2. Combined supports 'begins S, completes G2.' Same publisher; animal-centrosome caveat is scoped correctly.","evidence_ids":["E_70c6108994","E_d79c940d49"]},{"fact_id":"F3","status":"VERIFIED","reason":"Sources state karyokinesis/mitosis proceeds through prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase (nuclear division), followed by cytokinesis as second portion. Scope and ordering match; same publisher only.","evidence_ids":["E_70c6108994","E_d79c940d49"]},{"fact_id":"F4","status":"VERIFIED","reason":"Prometaphase passage supports nuclear envelope fragmentation, chromosome condensation into discrete structures, kinetochore formation at centromeric region, and sister kinetochores orienting to opposite poles. All claims entailed within prometaphase scope.","evidence_ids":["E_70c6108994"]},{"fact_id":"F5","status":"VERIFIED","reason":"Passage explicitly places M/spindle checkpoint near end of metaphase, checking sister chromatid attachment to spindle microtubules, and states cycle will not proceed until kinetochores are anchored to fibers from opposite poles. Entailed.","evidence_ids":["E_d79c940d49"]},{"fact_id":"F6","status":"VERIFIED","reason":"Telophase passage states chromosomes reach opposite poles and decondense, mitotic spindles break down, and nuclear envelopes form around chromosomes. Directly entailed.","evidence_ids":["E_d79c940d49"]},{"fact_id":"F7","status":"VERIFIED","reason":"One passage states cytokinesis physically separates cytoplasmic components into two daughter cells; another explicitly says interphase and mitosis can occur without cytokinesis producing multinucleate cells. Both parts supported. Same publisher.","evidence_ids":["E_70c6108994","E_d79c940d49"]},{"fact_id":"F8","status":"VERIFIED","reason":"PMID_27587616 abstract describes mitotic spindle as bipolar machine of microtubules plus associated proteins, requiring motor enzymes, separating duplicated chromosomes into two distinct sets.
